newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares finish with losses in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: KL shares finish with losses in thin trading.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips finished with losses in thin trading on Wednesday, as prevailing negative sentiment kept buying interest at a low ebb.
"Volume on the KLSE has gone down tremendously," said Leong Yoon Siang, of TA Securities' international division. "That means sellers are out, but buyers are not doing anything."

After an early gain on the Dow's surge evaporated, the Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks headed south and ended slightly above its session low of 1,108.97. It closed down 10.90 points or 0.97 percent to 1,109.60. Turnover totalled 219 million shares, with gainers nosing ahead by 295 to 266.
Against the blue chip losses, the Second Board index of small-capitalisation shares advanced by 1.31 points to 569.29. The broad KLSE EMAS index slipped 1.36 points to 319.21.

Analysts said the Composite Index will trade in a tight range over the next few weeks. Tony Shue, a vice president of institutional sales at Jupiter Securities, said he expects the Composite Index to be stuck between 1,080 and 1,140.

He said that while there was a small buy program this week in the market, "sentiment has changed for the worse versus six to seven weeks ago", adding, "there's no good news to make people change their minds."
